name: American modern high gain (rectifier-style)
notes: Modern American high-gain style: huge, saturated, scooped, with a spongy tube-rectifier feel. Path: gate -> V1a -> gain pot with bright cap -> V1b -> cold clipper stage -> V2b -> cathode follower -> tone stack -> master -> phase inverter -> 2x 6L6GC with light feedback and strong presence. FROM SCHEMATICS (fairly sure): cascaded 12AX7 stages with 100k plate resistors, one cold-biased 'clipper' stage, cathode follower into a passive tone stack, 6L6-family power tubes, tube rectifier option. UNSURE / APPROXIMATED: all cathode and bias values (cold clipper set to -3 V), the small coupling caps that tighten the bass (as high-passes at 150 and 200 Hz), the bright cap (+6 dB shelf at 1 kHz), tone stack slope resistor (47k) and treble cap (500 pF), feedback amount (set for about 5 dB), the power supply values (see below). Phase inverter as one triode that gets half the input (each triode of the real long-tailed pair sees half the signal, so it has twice the headroom of a single stage). POWER SUPPLY: two 5U4G tube rectifiers in parallel plus the winding, as 200 ohm into 47 uF (supply_ohms, supply_uf on the power block), so the sag comes from the current the power tubes really draw. These two values are GUESSES from typical parts, not from this amp's schematic. (It replaced a sag block.) COUPLING: every tube stage STARTS with its coupling capacitor into its grid resistor (coupling_nf, grid_ohms; default 22 nF into 1 Mohm = 7.2 Hz; power tubes 22 nF into 220k = 33 Hz), a 1st-order high-pass, and its bias shift recovers in C x R through that same capacitor (the guessed release times are gone). The small capacitors of tight stages (0.6-2 nF, from the old 80-250 Hz high-passes) recover in 1-2 ms: that is why tight amps use them. The output transformer's low end stays a post highpass1. The cathode follower is DC-coupled to v2b's plate (coupling_nf 0) and drives the tone stack directly; the tone stack's capacitors block the DC. PREAMP SUPPLY: every gain stage (v1a, v1b, v2a_cold, v2b, cathode_follower, pi) hangs on the same supply through decoupling filters (preamp_targets), so it sags too, about 100 ms behind (preamp_filter_ms: a GUESS; real amps have 10k-ish resistors and 10-50 uF capacitors per node). OUTPUT TRANSFORMER: the core of a 100 W amp's transformer, saturating on full-power notes below about 30 Hz (transformer_sat_hz: a GUESS from the amp's size, not measured): loud low notes lose bass and get odd harmonics. POWER TUBES: four (pairs 2) into half the load (2100 ohm), as in the 100 W originals: each tube works as in one pair, so the clipping is the same; the supply feeds twice the current, so it sags more (the supply values were guessed for one pair and are still GUESSES).
